subject: general
question: The vernacular Press Act proposed by _______ was intended to prevent the vernacular press from expressing criticism of British policies.
solution:
The correct answer is Lord Lytton.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The vernacular Press Act proposed by Lord Lytton was intended to prevent the vernacular press from expressing criticism of British policies. 
 
• He also passed the Arms Act 1878 which prohibited Indians from carrying weapons of any kind without licenses. Englishmen were excluded from this act.
 
• Vernacular Press Act of 1878: disallowing Indians from possessing arms and allowing the government to confiscate newspaper printing assets if anything objectionable was printed against the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Withdrawal of all ordinances issued by the Government of India imposing curbs on the activities of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Withdrawal of all prosecutions relating to several types of political offences (Rowlatt Act) except those involving violence. Release of prisoners arrested for participating in the Salt March.
 
• Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy, produced their scheme of constitutional reforms, known as the Montagu-Chelmsford (or Mont-Ford) Reforms, which led to the enactment of the Government of India Act 1919.
 
• The Mountbatten plan led to the royal assent for the approval of the Indian Independence Act 1947. Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy of India, came up with a plan under which he proposed that the provinces be declared independent successor states.
